style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm of the near miss. It is built on a counterfactual the congregation is told to say out loud -- had the LORD not been on our side. Then it walks through what would have happened: swallowed alive by the beast's mouth, swept away by the torrent, drowned in seething waters. Then the blessing breaks in: blessed be the LORD, who did not hand us over as prey to their teeth. The picture changes one more time, to one of the most defenceless creatures in the Psalter: our soul has escaped like a bird from the fowler's trap; the trap is broken, and we -- we have escaped. The last line became the votum -- the sentence with which Calvin's Geneva, and the Continental Reformed churches after it, have opened worship for nearly five centuries: our help is in the name of the LORD, who made the heavens and the earth. A psalm for everyone who has looked back at what almost happened and understood, only afterward, Who was standing there.

1.text: A song of ascents, of David. Had the LORD not been on our side -- let Israel now say it --
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth] of David. If [lule] it had not been the LORD [YHWH] who was on our side, now may Israel [Yisrael] say [amar];
1.notes: lule YHWH she-hayah lanu (H3884, H3068): 'if not for the LORD who was for us' -- the counterfactual the whole psalm hangs from -- yomar-na Yisrael (H559, H3478): let Israel SAY it -- the congregation is handed the line, as in Psalm 118:2, and told to repeat it.

2.text: had the LORD not been on our side when men rose up against us,
2.amp: If [lule] it had not been the LORD [YHWH] who was on our side, when men [adam] rose up [qum] against us:
2.notes: lule YHWH she-hayah lanu (H3884), 'if not for the LORD who was for us', again, now with the occasion: be-qum alenu adam (H6965, H120) -- when adam, mere humanity, rose against us. The double 'if not' is the psalm's suspense; the 'then's follow.

3.text: then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger blazed against us;
3.amp: Then [azay] they had swallowed us up [bala] quick [chay -- alive], when their wrath [aph] was kindled [charah -- burned] against us:
3.notes: azay chayyim belaunu (H233, H2416, H1104): THEN alive they would have swallowed us -- bala, the verb of the earth swallowing Korah and the fish swallowing Jonah -- ba-charot appam banu (H2734, H639): when their nose burned against us, the Hebrew idiom for fury.

4.text: then the waters would have washed us away; the torrent would have swept over our soul;
4.amp: Then [azay] the waters [mayim] had overwhelmed [shataph -- flooded, swept] us, the stream [nachal -- torrent, wadi] had gone over [abar] our soul [nephesh]:
4.notes: azay ha-mayim shetaphunu (H233, H4325, H7857): the second 'then': waters sweeping -- nachlah abar al-naphshenu (H5158, H5674, H5315): the nachal, the flash-flooding wadi that drowns travelers in a dry riverbed, passing over the soul. The enemy as a monster's mouth (v. 3), then as a flood.

5.text: then the seething, insolent waters would have swept over our soul.
5.amp: Then [azay] the proud [zeidon -- raging, seething] waters [mayim] had gone over [abar] our soul [nephesh].
5.notes: azay abar al-naphshenu ha-mayim ha-zedonim (H233, H5674, H5315, H4325, H2121): the third 'then' -- 'passed over our soul' -- and the waters are zedonim -- seething, insolent, the same root as the proud men of Psalm 86:14. The flood has a personality; it is the enemies' arrogance in liquid form.

6.text: Blessed be the LORD, who did not hand us over as prey to their teeth.
6.amp: Blessed [barak] be the LORD [YHWH], who has not given [natan] us as a prey [tereph] to their teeth [shen].
6.notes: barukh YHWH (H1288, H3068): the counterfactual breaks off and the blessing begins -- she-lo netananu tereph le-shinnehem (H5414, H2964, H8127): He did not GIVE us as prey to their teeth: the beast's mouth of verse 3 was open and God did not feed us to it.

7.text: Our soul has escaped like a bird from the fowler's trap; the trap is broken, and we -- we have escaped.
7.amp: Our soul [nephesh] is escaped [malat] as a bird [tsippor] out of the snare [pach] of the fowlers [yaqosh]: the snare is broken [shabar], and we are escaped [malat].
7.notes: naphshenu ke-tsippor nimletah mi-pach yoqeshim (H5315, H6833, H4422, H6341, H3369): the soul as a small bird out of the fowler's spring-trap -- Psalm 91:3's pach -- ha-pach nishbar va-anachnu nimlatnu (H7665): the trap BROKEN, not merely opened, and 'we' emphatic: we got out. Twice malat, escape: the psalm's happiest word.

8.text: Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made the heavens and the earth.
8.amp: Our help [ezer] is in the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH], who made [asah] heaven [shamayim] and earth [eretz].
8.notes: ezrenu be-shem YHWH (H5828, H8034, H3068): help in the Name -- oseh shamayim va-aretz (H6213, H8064, H776): Maker of heaven and earth, Psalm 121:2's and 134:3's credential. The line Calvin's Genevan liturgy, and many Reformed churches since, open worship with: the birds that escaped the trap know exactly Whose Name did it.
